descriptions.description: Illustrative record (fictional study) showing how a communication and humanities study of public online posts is described with HuMeta: no direct participants, social media sources, and online data practices.

Study design: Qualitative; Time series. Research questions: How do people describe climate anxiety in public posts, and how has this changed since 2018? Theoretical framework: Semiotics and Visual Rhetoric. Sampling: Non-probability: purposive / criterion-based. Data collection: Web or platform data collection (API, scraping, data donation); Assembling a corpus of texts, images, or media (e.g., published works, news). Analysis: Discourse or conversation analysis; Content analysis; Computational text or media analysis (e.g., text mining, NLP, image recognition). Sources: Social media and online platform content. Sources: About 12,000 public posts in English selected by keyword, with replies. Held at: Two public social media platforms (collected through their research APIs) Period covered: 2018-2023 Participants: Authors of public posts that mention climate anxiety; no authors were contacted. Kind of data (DDI): Mixed. Universe: Public English-language posts about climate anxiety on two social platforms, 2018-2023; excludes private and deleted posts. Weighting: No weights; the corpus is a purposive keyword sample, not a probability sample. Languages of the sources: en.

Ethics and access (HuMeta profile). Human participants: Indirectly: data are about people who do not take part (records, public online posts). Human-subjects review: Exempt determination. Participation consent: Not applicable. Consent for data sharing: Not applicable (no human-subjects data). Identifiability: Coded / pseudonymous (a linking key exists). Access level: Controlled access (application and/or data-use agreement). Online data: Content was publicly available (no login or membership needed); Collected under the platform's terms of service or a data-access agreement; Consent not sought (public content; ethics review agreed or determined not needed); Usernames and profile details removed or replaced; Quotes paraphrased or altered so authors cannot be found by searching; Only post IDs or derived data are shared, not the content itself; Content later deleted by its authors is removed from the dataset. Sensitivity: Public online content that can be traced to its authors. Only post IDs and derived codes are shared; researchers rehydrate posts under the platforms' terms.
CARE statement (HuMeta profile). Indigenous data: No.
